original_question: Let p be a prime and let G be a pro-p group. Suppose that all of the(continuous Galois) cohomology groups H n(G, Fp) of G with coefficients in the field of p elements are finite. Does it necessarily follow that the cohomology ring H ∗ (G, Fp) is finitely generated? The answer is known to be ‘yes’ if G is abelian-by-(p-adic analytic), as follows from(J. King, Commun. Algebra, 27, no. 10(1999), 4969–4991).
target_in_paper: Problem 21.78 in the section "New Problems (21st issue, 2026)" (posed by P. Kropholler): whether, for a pro-p group G, finiteness of all cohomology groups H^n(G, F_p) forces the cohomology ring H^*(G, F_p) to be finitely generated. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft is already extremely close to the paper-faithful formulation: it has the correct ambient objects (a prime p and a pro-p group G), the right hypothesis (all H^n(G, F_p) are finite), the right conclusion (finite generation of H^*(G, F_p)), and it preserves the paper’s contextual note that the answer is known to be yes for abelian-by-(p-adic analytic) groups via J. King. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))
missing_details: State explicitly that the hypothesis is quantified over every cohomological degree n >= 0; the paper says "all of the cohomology groups H^n(G, F_p)". ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))

Make explicit that H^n(G, F_p) means continuous cohomology of the profinite group G with coefficients in the discrete trivial G-module F_p; the paper says "(continuous Galois) cohomology" but leaves these conventions implicit. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))

Spell out that H^*(G, F_p) denotes the graded ring ⊕_{n>=0} H^n(G, F_p), with multiplication given by cup product; this is standard but implicit in the problem statement. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))

Clarify that "finitely generated" means finitely generated as an F_p-algebra (equivalently, in the graded cohomological sense relevant here), since the paper simply says "cohomology ring ... is finitely generated". ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))
refined_question: Let p be a prime and let G be a pro-p group. Assume that, for every n >= 0, the continuous cohomology group H^n(G, F_p) with coefficients in the discrete trivial G-module F_p is finite. Must the mod-p cohomology ring H^*(G, F_p) = ⊕_{n>=0} H^n(G, F_p), under cup product, be finitely generated as an F_p-algebra?
justification: This draft is essentially a near-verbatim restatement of Problem 21.78, so the correct refinement is not to broaden it but only to make its standard cohomological conventions explicit. I therefore kept the scope exactly at pro-p groups and the finite-generation question for mod-p continuous cohomology. I did not supply an alternate formulation, because the only nearby related statement in the paper is that a positive answer to Problem 21.80 would imply a positive answer to 21.78; that is a one-way implication, not an equivalence. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))
